summary:
Jezero Explorer is an interactive 3-D simulation built entirely on real NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance mission datasets. We developed a realistic exploration experience featuring 14 × 7 km of Jezero Crater terrain reconstructed from MRO HiRISE stereo elevation, authentic rocker-bogie rover kinematics, and Ingenuity aerial scouting flights.
Addressing the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge, the platform trains explorers to navigate precarious Martian threats. Users monitor extreme diurnal temperature swings, dust storm opacity, and solar irradiance, while identifying terrain hazards such as steep crater walls and wheel-trapping megaripples. A built-in Apollo-calibrated metabolic path planner calculates astronaut oxygen consumption, slope-adjusted exertion rates, and daylight return windows to prevent life-support exhaustion during suited Marswalk EVAs. We also created our own deterministic upscaling algorithm calibrated on Ingenuity and Perseverance draped on a topographic map.
Most space simulators reduce extraterrestrial survival to arcade games, while real planetary data remains locked in dense academic papers. Jezero Explorer bridges that gap. It turns raw NASA telemetry into an intuitive, accessible survival proving ground—teaching future explorers, engineers, and students the exact physiological, geological, and atmospheric constraints required to live and work on the surface of Mars.
details:
Jezero Explorer is an interactive, browser-based 3D simulation and operational survival guide that places users directly inside Mars's Jezero Crater. Built using WebGL (Three.js), it operates across four interconnected layers of planetary exploration:

  • Real Topography & Mobility Simulation: Recreates 14 × 7 km of Jezero Crater using true-scale MRO HiRISE stereo elevation models (DTMs). Users pilot the Perseverance rover with authentic rocker-bogie kinematic suspension, tilt limits (30° driver avoid / 45° rollover threshold), and realistic wheel sink, or launch the Ingenuity helicopter for rapid aerial scouting.
  • Apollo-Calibrated Marswalk EVA Planner: A tactical route planner that assesses surface safety before an astronaut steps foot outside. It calculates slope, surface roughness, and boulder hazards, adjusting astronaut walking pace based on real Apollo lunar expedition benchmarks (0.9 m/s level ground, 0.6 m/s at 8° incline, 0.14 m/s at 15° steep climb). It models metabolic oxygen consumption, required rest intervals, and return windows before sunset to output clear GO / CAUTION / NO-GO survival assessments.
  • 4-Sample Retrieval Campaign ("Operation Ground Truth"): A narrative-driven survival mission tracking real Perseverance drill sites: Tube 01 (Roubion atmospheric gas), Tube 02 (Montdenier volcanic basalt), Tube 09 (Séítah olivine within treacherous megaripples), and Tube 25 (Sapphire Canyon at Cheyava Falls—holding organic "leopard spots" biosignature candidates).
  • Dynamic Environmental Engine: Simulates real-time Martian solar illumination, Phobos and Deimos celestial tracks from NASA Horizons ephemerides, dust optical depth (τ\tauτ), and diurnal air temperature swings (-80°C to 0°C) from the rover's MEDA weather station.

What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Install Accessibility: Requires no bulky game engine installations or downloads; runs at 60 FPS directly in modern web browsers across desktops, laptops, tablets, and mobile devices.
  • Data-Grounded Survival Realism: Rather than relying on arbitrary game rules, survival parameters are derived directly from validated spaceflight telemetry, teaching users real planetary science principles.
  • Human-Robotic Synergies: Demonstrates how robotic vanguard assets (uncrewed rovers and aerial drones) de-risk astronaut survival by testing terrain firmness and scouting safe travel corridors before humans commit life-support resources.
  • Transparent Science Communication: Implements a strict "Ground Truth" policy—every data point in the UI clearly badges whether it is NASA Measured, Derived Model, or Simulated Game Rule.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Demystifying Extraterrestrial Operations: Bridges the gap between complex planetary datasets (PDS rasters, telemetry tables) and intuitive, hands-on spatial understanding.
  • Inspiring the Moon-to-Mars Generation: Serves as an educational tool for schools, universities, and space enthusiasts, demonstrating the real physiological, physical, and logistical hurdles of establishing a permanent human presence on Mars.
  • Open-Source Planetary Framework: Provides an extensible foundation for researchers and developers to visualize future landing sites, rover traverses, and crewed expedition architectures.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Architecture: Modern JavaScript (ES Modules), HTML5, CSS3 with modern glassmorphic UI design.
    • NASA MRO HiRISE: High-resolution stereo Digital Terrain Model and orthophoto mosaic of Jezero Crater.
    • NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Archive: Rover 3D CAD models, traverse coordinates, sample manifests, and core photography.
    • NASA MEDA (Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer): Real surface air temperature and dust optical depth records.
    • NASA JPL Horizons System: Celestial ephemeris trajectories for Sun, Phobos, and Deimos.
    • USGS SIM 3464: Jezero Crater regional geological unit maps.
    • Apollo Surface Mission Records: Astronaut metabolic exertion and slope pacing velocity curves.

How is your project creative?

  • Active Spectrometry Gamification: Instead of treating science as a passive pop-up, the laboratory challenges players to manually adjust spectrometer drift.
  • Seamless Multi-Modal Perspective: Players seamlessly switch between an orbital 2D mission control map, a ground-level third-person rover driving view, a first-person suited astronaut Marswalk, and high-altitude Ingenuity flight reconnaissance.
  • Gamifying Risk Management: Turns terrain science (slope gradients, regolith grain size) into critical tactical dilemmas—forcing players to decide whether to risk heavy rover wheel-spin in Séítah dunes or disembark on foot to preserve life support.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Physiological & Environmental Constraints: Thermal extremes (-80°C dusk), solar elevation, dust storm attenuation, oxygen burn rates, and slope-induced fatigue.
  • Hardware Limitations & Mobility Physics: Rover center-of-mass tilt limits, wheel torque degradation on loose regolith, and Ingenuity's thin-atmosphere rotor dynamics.
  • Web Performance & Memory Optimization: Implemented quadtree level-of-detail (LOD) streaming, texture mipmapping, adaptive screen resolution scaling, and memory garbage collection to ensure smooth rendering even on low-power mobile GPUs.
  • Realism vs. Playability: Balanced 1:1 realism (where Perseverance's actual speed of 4.2 cm/s would feel unplayable) by implementing adjustable time-warp factors (1× to 60×) while keeping on-foot EVA pacing locked strictly to real Apollo human physiological rates.
